sharing.allow_public_links_hint: Members may create restricted bearer links that do not require account sign-in for allowed resources.

sharing.allow_public_dashboards_hint: Higher risk. The public view restricts queries, variables, time ranges, and navigation.
sharing.max_expiry_hint: Creators cannot choose an expiration beyond this limit.
sharing.report_password: Require a password for public reports
sharing.report_password_hint: A short-lived share session is issued only after password verification.
sharing.deny_production: Block public sharing for production resources
sharing.deny_production_hint: Reject public links for resources tagged production or prod.
sharing.allow_csv_download_hint: When off, CSV reports can only be previewed in the restricted page.

danger.platform_only: Deleting an organization takes the Delete organization permission, which you do not have.
danger.delete_own_description: Deletes this organization and everything in it, for everyone. It cannot be undone.
danger.delete_confirm_description: Its members lose access, and everything in it is deleted and cannot be recovered. You will be signed out.

fields.name: Name

fields.oidc_redirect_uri_hint: Register this URL as an allowed callback at the OIDC identity provider. It is derived from the MoleSignal external URL.
fields.saml_callback_url_hint: Register this URL as the Assertion Consumer Service URL at the SAML identity provider. It is derived from the MoleSignal external URL.
fields.ldap_url_hint: Use ldaps://, or ldap:// with StartTLS enabled
fields.start_tls_hint: Required for ldap://; disable for ldaps://
fields.user_filter_hint: Must include {username}; the value is escaped before search
fields.bind_pair_hint: Leave both bind fields empty only when anonymous search is allowed
fields.discover_hint: Reads the issuer's .well-known/openid-configuration and fills in the endpoints below.
fields.discovered: Endpoints filled in from the discovery document
fields.endpoints_pending: The endpoints appear once the fields above are filled in.
fields.oauth2_userinfo_hint: After sign-in this endpoint is read with the access token, and the field mapping picks the account out of it.
fields.sp_entity_id_hint: How the identity provider knows MoleSignal; defaults to the instance address.

mapping.oidc_hint: Map MoleSignal identity fields to OIDC claims. Dot-separated paths such as realm_access.roles are supported; separate several sources with | to take the first that has a value.
mapping.saml_hint: Map MoleSignal identity fields to SAML Attribute names. Use NameID to read the assertion subject.
mapping.ldap_hint: Map MoleSignal identity fields to LDAP attributes. Use dn to read the matched entry DN.
mapping.default_role_hint: Applied when no external group mapping matches. If omitted, the self-service signup role is used.
mapping.roles_empty: This organization has no assignable roles. Create an organization role in IAM first.
mapping.roles_unavailable: The role list is not available yet
mapping.group_roles_hint: Each matching external group grants the selected MoleSignal role. Bindings are synchronized at sign-in.
mapping.oauth2_hint: Map MoleSignal identity fields to the JSON the user endpoint returns. Dot-separated paths are supported; separate several sources with | to take the first that has a value.
mapping.github_fixed: GitHub is read in a fixed way: the subject is the account's numeric ID, the email is the verified primary address, and groups are organizations (my-org) and teams (my-org/sre).
mapping.no_groups: This platform sends no groups, so every account that signs in gets the default role.

inputs.tenant_id_hint: Copy it from the app registration's Overview page.
inputs.authorization_server_hint: The ID of a custom authorization server; leave empty for the org authorization server.

hints.google: In the Google Cloud console, create an OAuth client ID (Web application) and add the redirect URI below to Authorized redirect URIs.
hints.microsoft: In the Microsoft Entra app registration, add a Web platform with the redirect URI, then create a client secret. The groups claim carries group object IDs.
hints.okta: In Okta, create an OIDC web app and add the redirect URI to Sign-in redirect URIs. To read groups, add a groups claim on the authorization server.
hints.auth0: In Auth0, create a Regular Web Application and add the redirect URI to Allowed Callback URLs. Auth0 sends no groups by itself: write them into a custom claim with an Action, then point the groups mapping at it.
hints.keycloak: In the realm, create an OpenID Connect client with Client authentication on and add the redirect URI to Valid redirect URIs. To read groups, add a Group Membership mapper with groups as the token claim name.
hints.authentik: Create an OAuth2/OpenID provider bound to an application and add the redirect URI to Redirect URIs. The application slug is on the application's page.
hints.gitlab: In GitLab's Applications, create an application with the openid, profile, and email scopes and the redirect URI as its callback URL.
hints.github: In GitHub's Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps, create an app with the redirect URI as its authorization callback URL. Where an organization restricts OAuth app access, an owner must approve the app before its organizations and teams can be read.
hints.feishu: In the Feishu open platform's custom app, add the redirect URL under Security settings and grant the permission to read user email under Permissions. The App ID and App Secret are the client ID and secret.
hints.microsoft_saml: In the enterprise application's Single sign-on, choose SAML: the identifier is the SP entity ID and the reply URL is the ACS URL. Then import its App Federation Metadata Url below.
hints.okta_saml: In Okta, create a SAML 2.0 app: the single sign-on URL is the ACS URL and the audience URI is the SP entity ID. Add email and displayName attribute statements and a groups group attribute statement.
hints.google_saml: In the Google Admin console, add a custom SAML app: the ACS URL and entity ID are the values below. Map email and name, and group membership to groups. Download the IdP metadata and paste it below.
hints.adfs: Add a relying party trust: the identifier is the SP entity ID and the SAML assertion consumer endpoint is the ACS URL (POST). Issue E-Mail Address, Name, and Token-Groups with claim rules.
hints.jumpcloud: Create a SAML app with the SP entity ID and ACS URL below. Add email and name user attributes and turn on Include group attribute (memberOf). Export the metadata and paste it below.
hints.active_directory: Users sign in with their Windows account name, UPN, or email. The search account only needs to read users and memberOf.
hints.openldap: Groups are read from memberOf, which needs the memberof overlay.
hints.freeipa: A read-only service account under cn=sysaccounts,cn=etc works for the search.

metadata.xml: Paste the metadata XML downloaded from the identity provider

access.title: Sign-in scope
access.allowed_groups_hint: When set, only accounts in one of these groups can sign in with this provider; empty allows every account.
access.public_missing: Anyone can create such an account. Before enabling it, add the organization's email domains or the groups allowed to sign in.
access.public_domains: New accounts can join only with an email address on {{domains}}.
access.public_groups: Only accounts in the allowed groups can sign in.
access.public_reason: Restrict email domains or allowed groups first

test.title: Test sign-in
test.hint: Goes through a real sign-in with the saved settings. No session starts, no account is created or linked, and your own sign-in stays as it is.
test.save_first: Save your changes first: a test runs on the saved settings.
test.toast_failed: “{{name}}” failed the test sign-in. Open its result to see why.

directory.title: Test sign-in · {{name}}
directory.description: Checks an account against the directory, the way a sign-in does. A wrong password counts toward the directory’s lockout policy and this instance’s sign-in limits. The password isn’t stored.

result.title: Test sign-in · {{name}}
result.passed_body: The sign-in went all the way through. Nothing changed: no session started, no account was created or linked, and no roles moved.
result.pending_body: Finish signing in on the other tab; this page updates by itself. If the identity provider shows an error there, it can’t reach this page. The usual cause is a redirect URI it doesn’t have registered.
result.expired_body: The identity provider didn’t send the browser back within 10 minutes. If it showed an error page, the usual cause is a redirect URI it doesn’t have registered. Check that, then test again.
result.stale_body: The provider’s settings changed after this test. Test again to check the current ones.
result.name: Name
result.subject: Subject
result.mapping_title: What a real sign-in would do

account.link_you: Your account {{email}} has this email, but this identity isn’t linked to it yet. Your first sign-in asks you to confirm, with your password or a code sent by email.
account.link_other: The account {{email}} has this email, but this identity isn’t linked to it yet. Its owner confirms at the first sign-in, with the password or a code sent by email.
account.create: No account has this email. The first sign-in creates {{email}}, without a password.
account.joins: It joins this workspace at that sign-in.

role_source.signup: What new members get: no group or default role applies
role_source.unchanged: Stays as it is: no group or default role applies

idp_error.title: The identity provider refused the sign-in
idp_error.advice: Read its message below. Usually the account isn’t assigned to this application, or a scope isn’t allowed.

no_code.title: The identity provider sent no authorization code
no_code.advice: Check that the application uses the authorization code flow, and that the authorization URL is right.

network.title: This server couldn’t reach the identity provider
network.advice: Check the token and user info URLs, and that this server can reach them through any proxy or firewall.

token_exchange.title: The identity provider refused the authorization code
token_exchange.advice: Check the client ID and client secret, and that the redirect URI is registered exactly as shown in the settings.

no_id_token.title: The identity provider returned no ID token
no_id_token.advice: Add the openid scope. If this provider doesn’t do OpenID Connect, set it up as OAuth 2.0 instead.

id_token_issuer.title: The ID token came from another issuer
id_token_issuer.advice: Set the issuer URL to the value in the provider’s discovery document, including its path.

id_token_audience.title: The ID token is for another application
id_token_audience.advice: Check that the client ID is the one of this application at the identity provider.

id_token_expired.title: The ID token has expired or isn’t valid yet
id_token_expired.advice: Check that the clocks of this server and the identity provider agree.

id_token_nonce.title: The ID token doesn’t belong to this sign-in
id_token_nonce.advice: Test again. If it keeps happening, the identity provider isn’t returning the nonce, or something between is caching its answer.

id_token_invalid.title: The ID token didn’t pass verification
id_token_invalid.advice: Check the JWKS URL and the signing algorithm. A token signed with the client secret needs that secret saved here.

jwks.title: The identity provider’s signing keys couldn’t be used
jwks.advice: Check the JWKS URL, and that this server can reach it.

userinfo.title: The user info request failed
userinfo.advice: Check the user info URL, and that the scopes allow reading the profile.

claim_missing.title: The identity provider didn’t return a mapped field
claim_missing.advice: The message below names it. Correct the identity field mapping, or add the scope or claim that carries the field.

saml_status.title: The identity provider answered with a failure
saml_status.advice: Read its message below. Usually the account isn’t assigned to this application.

saml_no_response.title: The callback carried no SAML response
saml_no_response.advice: Check that the identity provider posts to the ACS URL shown in the settings.

saml_malformed.title: The SAML response couldn’t be read
saml_malformed.advice: Check that the identity provider sends a signed assertion with the HTTP-POST binding.

saml_certificate.title: The signing certificate doesn’t match
saml_certificate.advice: Copy the current signing certificate from the identity provider, or read its metadata again.

saml_signature.title: The assertion’s signature didn’t verify
saml_signature.advice: The assertion itself must be signed, not only the response. Check the signing settings and the certificate.

saml_time.title: The assertion is outside its validity window
saml_time.advice: Check that the clocks of this server and the identity provider agree.

saml_audience.title: The assertion is for another service
saml_audience.advice: Set the audience at the identity provider to this provider’s SP entity ID.

saml_recipient.title: The assertion is for another address
saml_recipient.advice: Set the ACS URL at the identity provider exactly as shown in the settings.

ldap_connect.title: This server couldn’t connect to the directory
ldap_connect.advice: Check the address, the port and the TLS settings, and that this server trusts the directory’s certificate.

ldap_service_bind.title: The directory refused the search account
ldap_service_bind.advice: Check the search bind DN and its password.

ldap_search.title: The user search failed
ldap_search.advice: Check the user base DN and the syntax of the search filter.

ldap_no_entry.title: No directory entry matches this account
ldap_no_entry.advice: Check the account name, the user base DN and the search filter.

ldap_many_entries.title: Several directory entries match this account
ldap_many_entries.advice: Narrow the search filter so it finds exactly one entry.

ldap_missing_attribute.title: The directory entry lacks a mapped attribute
ldap_missing_attribute.advice: The message below names it. Correct the identity field mapping.

ldap_rejected.title: The directory refused this password
ldap_rejected.advice: Check the password, and whether the account is locked or has expired. This attempt counts toward the directory’s lockout policy.

group_not_allowed.title: This account isn’t in an allowed group
group_not_allowed.advice: Add it to one of the allowed groups, or change the list. If the provider returned no groups above, check the groups field mapping and the scopes.

email_unverified.title: The identity provider hasn’t verified this email
email_unverified.advice: Verify it at the identity provider: a provider open to public accounts only lets in verified addresses.

provider_unrestricted.title: This provider accepts public accounts without a limit
provider_unrestricted.advice: Add the organization’s email domains, or the groups allowed to sign in.

invalid_email.title: The email the provider returned isn’t an address
invalid_email.advice: Map the email field to a claim that holds an address.

email_domain.title: This email’s domain can’t join the workspace
email_domain.advice: Add the domain under Email domains, or sign in with an address on an allowed domain.

org_disabled.title: This workspace is disabled
org_disabled.advice: A platform administrator has to enable it first.

account_unavailable.title: The account this identity maps to can’t sign in
account_unavailable.advice: It is disabled, waiting for approval or was rejected. Check it under Users.

account_confined.title: This account belongs to another organization’s single sign-on
account_confined.advice: Its owner has to verify the email, by resetting the password, before it can join here.

role_missing.title: The role binding names a role that no longer exists
role_missing.advice: Edit the provider and choose an existing role.

directory_blocked.title: This workspace only allows single sign-on
directory_blocked.advice: Directory sign-ins can’t enter while “Only allow single sign-on” is on.

settings_changed.title: The settings changed during this test
settings_changed.advice: Test again with the saved settings.

unknown.title: The test didn’t go through
unknown.advice: Check the message below, if there is one, and the provider’s settings, then test again.

notes.no_groups: The provider returned no groups, so the role binding has nothing to match. Check the groups field mapping and the scopes.
notes.groups_unmapped: None of these groups is in the role binding.
notes.another_account: This isn’t the account you’re using now. Test with your own to see that you can still get in.
notes.roles_change: Signing in replaces this member’s roles with the ones shown. Check that an administrator keeps enough access.
notes.second_factor: A real sign-in also asks this account for a second factor.

signin_requirements.title: Sign-in requirements
signin_requirements.subtitle: What entering this workspace asks of a sign-in. Changes reach every session within 15 minutes.
signin_requirements.platform_subtitle: What entering the platform organization asks of a sign-in. Changes reach every session within 15 minutes.
signin_requirements.mfa_description: Entering this workspace takes multi-factor authentication. Members who haven’t turned it on set it up at their next sign-in; for members coming through this workspace’s single sign-on, the identity provider is responsible.
signin_requirements.mfa_platform: Entering the platform organization takes multi-factor authentication. Accounts that haven’t turned it on set it up at their next sign-in.
signin_requirements.sso_description: The only way in is this workspace’s OIDC, OAuth 2.0 or SAML provider: account passwords, passkeys and LDAP can’t enter. The root user is the exception, to get in when the identity provider is down.
signin_requirements.sso_unavailable: Enable an OIDC, OAuth 2.0 or SAML provider first.
signin_requirements.mfa_confirm_description: Within 15 minutes, every session without multi-factor authentication has to sign in again, yours included. Members who haven’t turned it on set it up as they sign in.
signin_requirements.sso_confirm_description: Within 15 minutes, every session that didn’t come through this workspace’s single sign-on has to sign in again, yours included, and database clients can no longer connect with an account password.
signin_requirements.last_provider: This workspace only allows single sign-on, and this is its last working provider. Turn off “Only allow single sign-on” first.
signin_requirements.sso_untested_note: No provider has passed a test sign-in with its current settings. Run one from the list below.
signin_requirements.sso_untested_title: Only allow single sign-on without a passing test?
signin_requirements.sso_untested_description: No provider of this workspace has passed a test sign-in with its current settings, so nothing shows that anyone can still get in. Cancel to test one first.
signin_requirements.fact_sessions_value: Within 15 minutes, every session that didn’t come through single sign-on ends, yours included.
signin_requirements.fact_clients_value: Database clients can no longer connect with an account password.
signin_requirements.fact_way_back_value: Only the root user can still get in with a password.

cipher_keys.title: Cipher keys
cipher_keys.subtitle: Encryption keys for at-rest column ciphering. Owner-only.
cipher_keys.empty_description: Create a key to enable column-level encryption on sensitive streams.
cipher_keys.delete_confirm_description: Data encrypted with this key will become unreadable.
cipher_keys.rotate_drawer_subtitle: Paste the new 32-byte base64-encoded key material.
cipher_keys.create_drawer_subtitle: Provide a name and 32-byte base64-encoded key material.

regex_patterns.title: Regex patterns
regex_patterns.subtitle: Reusable regex shortcuts, also used for sensitive-data masking.
regex_patterns.empty_description: Create reusable regex shortcuts for VRL transforms.
regex_patterns.field_replacement_hint: Matched text is replaced with this. Supports $1 capture groups; leave empty to delete the match.
regex_patterns.field_apply_on_intake_hint: Permanently redact matches at write time. When off, only the mask(col) query function applies this rule.

domain_management.subtitle: Custom domains with managed TLS certificates.
domain_management.empty_description: Add a hostname to terminate TLS for this org.
domain_management.delete_confirm_description: TLS termination for this hostname will stop.

organization_management.title: Organization management
organization_management.subtitle: Manage tenant organizations from the _sys workspace.
organization_management.empty_description: Create the first tenant organization for this MoleSignal instance.
organization_management.create_drawer_subtitle: Platform administrators create tenant organizations from _sys.
organization_management.form_invalid: Enter both a workspace name and slug.
organization_management.enable_description: Restore access to {{name}} and allow its members and credentials to use the organization again.
organization_management.disable_description: Pause access to {{name}} immediately. Existing sessions and API credentials will be rejected until it is enabled again.
organization_management.last_enabled: At least one tenant organization must remain enabled.

organization_management.delete_disabled: The system organization is immutable, and at least one tenant organization must remain.

nodes.title: Nodes / remote clusters
nodes.subtitle: Manage the local data plane, cluster federation, and remote query targets.

service_graph.title: Service data source
service_graph.subtitle: Control how the service map is built from traces for single-node or multi-intake deployments.
service_graph.storage_hint: A single node periodically rebuilds the service map from stored traces. Results are correct across nodes with a 1–2 minute delay.
service_graph.intake_hint: Each intake process pairs spans in memory and flushes them. Latency is low, but spans split across nodes may be undercounted.

client_ip.title: Client IP recognition
client_ip.subtitle: Choose how this deployment identifies client addresses for RUM, sign-in limits, and the audit of public links. Proxy headers are trusted only when the TCP peer matches an approved CIDR.
client_ip.resolver_subtitle: This database-backed setting is shared by the deployment and refreshes across collector nodes without restarting them.

mode_hints.peer: Uses the TCP peer address and ignores all forwarding headers. This is the secure default for a directly exposed collector.
mode_hints.header: Reads one bare IP from the configured header, but only for requests arriving from a trusted proxy.
mode_hints.forwarded_chain: Walks the configured IP chain from right to left, skips trusted proxies, and selects the first untrusted address.

client_ip.header_hint: Use a dedicated CDN or proxy header. Authorization, Cookie, API key, and client-certificate headers are blocked.
client_ip.trusted_cidrs_hint: One IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR per line, up to 64. Wildcard /0 networks are accepted, but trust every connection source in that address family; use them only behind a protected ingress. The header is ignored when the connection peer is outside these networks.
client_ip.chain_strategy_hint: The strategy is fixed to rightmost_untrusted. The second field limits the number of addresses accepted from a request (1–64).
client_ip.fallback_hint: Use the TCP peer if the trusted header is missing, malformed, too long, or has no usable client address.
client_ip.allow_private_hint: Accept private, loopback and link-local addresses from a trusted header, and count them as sources for sign-in limits. Turn on when people connect from a private network. Leave off behind a proxy you haven’t set up here: everyone would count as one address.

validation.chain_length: Maximum chain length must be a whole number from 1 to 64.
validation.header: Enter a valid, non-sensitive HTTP header name (maximum 128 characters).
validation.cidrs: Enter 1–64 trusted IPv4 or IPv6 CIDRs, one per line.

federation.title: Cluster federation
federation.subtitle: Synchronize resource changes across clusters. Advanced parameters save together, and disabling federation requires confirmation.
federation.disable_confirm_description: Sending and receiving cross-cluster resource changes will stop. Existing local data is not affected.

hints.cluster_id: A stable, unique identifier for this cluster. It must be unique in the federation and remain unchanged across restarts. Leave blank to disable federation.

nodes.empty_description: Add a remote cluster to enable federated search.
nodes.delete_confirm_description: Federated queries will no longer fan out to this target.
nodes.field_token_secret_hint: Reference to secret manager — inline tokens rejected.

org_map.title: Org mappings
org_map.description: Map this cluster's orgs to local orgs for cross-cluster config sync. Unmapped orgs are rejected on receive.
org_map.field_token_hint: Optional. env:VAR or cipher_keys:<id>. Falls back to the cluster token.

ai_toolsets.title: AI toolsets
ai_toolsets.subtitle: Registered tools Mole Agent can call.
ai_toolsets.empty_description: Register constrained tools when Mole Agent is enabled.
ai_toolsets.builtin_hint: Only the checked built-in tools are exposed to the model for this org. Leave all checked to allow everything.
ai_toolsets.custom_hint: Define tools that proxy to your own HTTP endpoint; the model calls them and the backend POSTs to the URL.

query_management.subtitle: In-flight queries and recent inspector activity.
query_management.already_cancelled: This query has already been cancelled.
query_management.empty_description: Long-running queries will appear here while they execute.

audit.subtitle_retention_days_one: Search the audit trail by time, actor, action, and target. Records are kept for {{count}} day.
audit.subtitle_retention_days_other: Search the audit trail by time, actor, action, and target. Records are kept for {{count}} days.

audit.change_retention_hint: Takes you to the platform organization, where audit retention is set.
audit.empty_description: No events match the current filters.
audit.views_page_hint: Among the records of this page
audit.load_error: Could not load the audit trail

audit_retention.title: Audit retention
audit_retention.subtitle: Audit records of every organization and of the platform are kept for the number of days set here.
audit_retention.days_hint: Older records are deleted once a day and cannot be recovered. Enter 0 to keep them forever.
audit_retention.invalid: Enter a whole number from 0 to 3650.

preview.counting: Counting the records this change would delete…

stream_retention.title: Data retention
stream_retention.subtitle: Streams without a retention of their own keep the default; the runs of synthetic checks keep their own number of days.
stream_retention.days_hint: Each stream can set its own retention in its settings. Data older than the retention is deleted in the next cleanup and cannot be recovered.

synthetic_retention.days_hint: Older runs, their artifacts and finished tasks are deleted once a day; 0 keeps them for good. The _synthetic_results stream that availability reads follows its own stream retention.
synthetic_retention.invalid: Enter a whole number from 0 to {{max}}.

series_limits.title: Metric cardinality
series_limits.subtitle: Limits how many series Prometheus writes may keep active at once, so high-cardinality labels cannot exhaust memory and storage.
series_limits.per_org_hint: How many series an organization may keep active at once. At the limit, writes of new series are rejected while existing series keep being written; a series without data for a while is no longer active.
series_limits.per_metric_hint: How many series one metric of an organization may keep active at once, at most the organization limit.
series_limits.invalid: Enter whole numbers from 1 to {{max}}, with the metric limit at most the organization limit.

signin_limits.title: Sign-in limits
signin_limits.subtitle: Stop password guessing without letting anyone lock someone else out. Passkeys and single sign-on aren’t counted or limited.
signin_limits.section_subtitle: Enter 0 to turn a count off. An unknown account counts like any other, so the answer never says whether an account exists. The access password of a public link counts the same way, with each link as one account.
signin_limits.account_source_hint: Failures before this address is locked out of this account. Nobody else is affected.
signin_limits.source_hint: Failures before this address can’t sign in with a password at all. People sharing the address are affected too.
signin_limits.account_hint: Failures before passwords for this account are slowed down. The account is never locked, and an address that signed in during the last 30 days isn’t slowed.
signin_limits.interval: While slowed down, check a password every
signin_limits.interval_hint: From 1 to 600 seconds. Attempts in between are told to try again later, without checking the password.
signin_limits.lock_hint: How long an address stays locked, and how far back failures count. Resetting the password unlocks the account at once.
signin_limits.source_counted: Failures from this address count against it.
signin_limits.source_private: This is a private address, so only the account limit applies. If people really connect from private addresses, turn on “Count private addresses as clients”.
signin_limits.source_proxy_public: This request carries forwarding headers, but the address is the connection’s. If MoleSignal is behind a proxy, everyone counts as this one address and they lock each other out. Set up trusted proxies.
signin_limits.source_proxy_private: This request carries forwarding headers, so MoleSignal is probably behind a proxy. Only the account limit applies until you set up trusted proxies.
signin_limits.source_none: No address could be read from this request, so only the account limit applies.
signin_limits.invalid: Enter whole numbers: failures from 0 to {{failures}}, seconds from 1 to {{seconds}}, minutes from 1 to {{minutes}}.

ai_providers.title: AI providers
ai_providers.subtitle: Model providers and encrypted API keys for AI investigation.
ai_providers.empty_description: Add an approved model provider to enable Mole Agent chat.
ai_providers.field_api_key_hint_create: Stored encrypted; shown only as last 4 digits after saving.
ai_providers.field_api_key_hint_edit: Leave blank to keep the existing key; use Rotate key to change it.

field_masking.title: Field masking
field_masking.subtitle: Global rules use first-match order; stream fields can override or disable inherited masking. Queries compute on raw values and mask only final results; metrics streams are excluded.
field_masking.empty_description: Create a global fallback rule or configure a stream-level field override.
field_masking.drawer_subtitle: The first matching rule wins. Drag rows to change priority.
field_masking.field_pattern_hint: Supports exact names and * or ? wildcards; regular expressions are not accepted.
field_masking.field_stream_pattern_hint: Leave empty for every stream; supports * and ? wildcards.
field_masking.field_replacement_hint: The matched region is replaced once with this value.

algorithm_hints.full: Replace the entire field with a fixed value.
algorithm_hints.inner: Keep a prefix and suffix while masking the middle.
algorithm_hints.outer: Keep only the [start, end) range and mask both sides.
algorithm_hints.hash: Create a deterministic digest with an organization-scoped backend-managed key.

ai_prompts.title: AI prompts
ai_prompts.subtitle: Built-in and custom prompt templates for AI investigation.
ai_prompts.empty_description: Built-in prompts should appear here once the backend is reachable.
ai_prompts.field_body_hint: Use {{variables}} allowed by this purpose; unknown variables are rejected.

alert_evaluation.title: Alert evaluation
alert_evaluation.subtitle: In a cluster split by role, queries read only what the intake nodes have written out. Alert rules look a little further back each round so recent data has been written.
alert_evaluation.delay_hint: When a rule sets no delay of its own, each round's window moves back this many seconds. A single process that runs every role moves nothing. Intake writes out every 30 seconds by default.
alert_evaluation.invalid: Enter a whole number from 0 to {{max}}.

holidays.title: Holiday calendars
holidays.subtitle: Days off and make-up workdays. Routing rules, alert pipelines, support hours, silences, rotations and notify policies can count by them; a date is read in the timezone of whatever uses the calendar.
holidays.empty_description: Add one, or import an ICS file of public holidays.
holidays.delete_in_use_one: Used by {{count}} place: {{names}}. Take it out there first.
holidays.delete_in_use_other: Used by {{count}} places: {{names}}. Take it out there first.
holidays.drawer_subtitle: A day off takes those days out of weekly hours; a make-up workday counts as a Monday.
holidays.import_hint: All-day events become days; a name with 补班, 上班 or ending in 班 becomes a make-up workday. Nothing is saved until you save the calendar.
holidays.imported_one: Read {{count}} day from the file. Check it and save.
holidays.imported_other: Read {{count}} days from the file. Check them and save.

importance.title: Priority and urgency
importance.subtitle: How many priority levels the organization uses and what they are called, and what each urgency level does when it pages.

errors.key: A key starts with a lowercase letter and has lowercase letters, digits and underscores.
errors.key_twice: Two urgency levels have the same key.
errors.built_in: The built-in levels high and low stay; they can be renamed.
errors.severities: Each severity goes to exactly one urgency level.

priorities.title: Priority levels
priorities.description: Keys stay P1, P2, …; integrations and imported files use them. A priority beyond the levels, from an alert or a pipeline, falls to the lowest one.
priorities.name: Name of {{priority}}

urgencies.title: Urgency levels
urgencies.description: The most urgent first. Each level says whether it climbs the policy, what quiet hours do, which of a person's two step groups it uses, and which severities go to it when a policy sets urgency by severity.
urgencies.name: Name of {{key}}
urgencies.built_in: Built in: it can be renamed, not removed.

intake_usage.title: Intake usage
intake_usage.subtitle: How long the record of what each source took in is kept, and how many services are counted apart.
intake_usage.retention_days_hint: Hourly records older than this are deleted once a day. At least 35 days, so that a monthly budget can always be read back.
intake_usage.max_services_hint: How many services an organization has counted apart in an hour, on each node. Past it, the rest are counted together as other services, so that a sender cannot grow the records by naming services.
intake_usage.invalid: Keep records for {{minDays}} to {{maxDays}} days, and count 1 to {{maxServices}} services.
